title: Practise Now 5
summary: Find the height above eye level, then add the eye height.
alt: Practise Now 5: Michael's eyes are 10 m from a tree and 1.8 m above the ground; the distance from his eyes to the top of the tree is 14 m. Find the height of the tree.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: Michael's eyes **E** are **10 m** (horizontally) from a tree and **1.8 m** above the ground. The distance from his eyes to the top **T** of the tree is **14 m**. With **F** level with his eyes, **∠F = 90°**. Find the height of the tree.

steps.title: Spot the right angle
steps.narration: In ΔETF, **∠F = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **ET**. The other two sides meet at the right angle.

steps.title: Pythagoras' theorem
steps.narration: **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{ET^2} &= \role{legA}{EF^2} + \role{legB}{h^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Make the unknown the subject
steps.narration: We want a **shorter side**, so subtract the known square from the hypotenuse square.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{ET^2} &= \role{legA}{EF^2} + \role{legB}{h^2} \\ \role{legB}{h^2} &= \role{hyp}{ET^2} - \role{legA}{EF^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute the lengths
steps.narration: Replace each side by its length.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{ET^2} &= \role{legA}{EF^2} + \role{legB}{h^2} \\ \role{legB}{h^2} &= \role{hyp}{ET^2} - \role{legA}{EF^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{14^2} - \role{legA}{10^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 96 is not a perfect square. Use a calculator and keep 4 significant figures — we need this value again.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{ET^2} &= \role{legA}{EF^2} + \role{legB}{h^2} \\ \role{legB}{h^2} &= \role{hyp}{ET^2} - \role{legA}{EF^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{14^2} - \role{legA}{10^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{196} - \role{legA}{100} \\ &= \role{legB}{96} \\ \role{legB}{h} &= \sqrt{96} = 9.798\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Add the eye height
steps.narration: The tree rises **h** above eye level, and Michael's eyes are **1.8 m** above the ground.\[\begin{aligned}\text{height of tree} &= 1.8 + 9.798\ldots \\ &= \role{ans}{11.6\ \text{m}}\quad(\text{3 s.f.})\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse **26 m** and one shorter side **10 m**. Find the other shorter side.

takeaways: Find the **right angle** first — the side opposite it is the **hypotenuse**.
To find a shorter side: **subtract** the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the **square root**.
A shorter side must be **smaller** than the hypotenuse — a quick check on your answer.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
